what_i_did: Read lab/TASKS.md, tasks/longhorizon/spec.md, the multi-mode examples in dev.json and the exact/number/regex checker code in lab/core.py.

Wrote a generator script (kept in the session scratchpad, not in the repo) that defines each task as a start list plus per-turn list operations and builds turns, checks, reference and negative from a python list simulator.

Wrote 21 multi-mode tasks (4-6 turns) covering join back/front, leave, serve one or several from the front, neighbour swaps, move to a position, insert next to a named item, name correction, set membership with no-op duplicates, reversal, rotation, overtakes, bulk leave.
how_answers_were_verified: Every final state and every echoed intermediate reply was computed by the simulator in strict mode (an operation that is invalid on the current list raises).
For each task the script asserted that the final answer differs from the answer at the start and after every earlier turn (no stale answer passes).

For each task the script asserted that dropping any single effective update changes the final answer; six first-draft tasks failed this and were redesigned. For the two auto-chosen position questions (g3-13, g3-17) the position was picked from those satisfying both assertions.
Each negative is the simulated outcome of dropping exactly one update.
Total turn text is under 900 characters per task (max 611).
not_done: No model was run on these tasks (held-out), so the easy/medium/hard labels are estimates from the spec's baseline observations, not measurements.
Did not read other generators' files.
